findings.quoted_text: Client may terminate this Agreement at any time, without notice and without further payment.
All intellectual property rights in each Deliverable transfer to Client upon delivery.
Invoices are payable Net 30. An invoice that remains unpaid after the due date may accrue interest at 1.0% per month to the extent permitted by applicable law.
Client may dispute an invoice in good faith by providing written details within 15 days. The undisputed portion remains payable when due.

The parties acknowledge that the description of the Services is intended to identify the principal workstreams. Minor clarifications may be made through ordinary project communications, provided that such clarification does not materially increase the workload.
Any post-launch support period is limited to the duration and scope stated in the commercial schedule. Requests outside that scope are handled as new Services or change requests.
At handover, Contractor will provide the agreed source files, credentials or access instructions that Contractor is entitled to transfer, and available documentation.
Client may terminate this Agreement at any time, without notice and without further payment.
findings.explanation: The client can end the contract whenever they wish and is not required to pay for any work already performed, leaving the contractor unpaid for services rendered.
findings.suggested_change: Add a provision that client termination requires at least 30 days written notice and payment for all work completed up to the termination date, including approved expenses and any earned milestones.

findings.quoted_text: All intellectual property rights in each Deliverable transfer to Client upon delivery.
findings.explanation: IP ownership shifts to the client before the contractor has received full payment for the deliverable, reducing leverage to enforce payment if the client delays or disputes invoices.
findings.suggested_change: Make the transfer of IP rights conditional upon receipt of payment for the corresponding invoice (or at least upon payment of a specified percentage, e.g., 50% of the deliverable fee).

findings.quoted_text: Invoices are payable Net 30. An invoice that remains unpaid after the due date may accrue interest at 1.0% per month to the extent permitted by applicable law.
findings.explanation: A 30‑day payment window can strain cash flow for a freelancer; the modest 1% monthly interest may not be a strong deterrent for late payment.
findings.suggested_change: Reduce the payment term to Net 15 and increase the late‑payment interest to 1.5% per month (or the maximum allowed by law) plus a reasonable fixed late fee.

findings.quoted_text: Client may dispute an invoice in good faith by providing written details within 15 days. The undisputed portion remains payable when due.
findings.explanation: The client can withhold up to 15 days of payment while disputing an invoice, which can delay cash flow and create uncertainty about when funds will be received.
findings.suggested_change: Shorten the dispute period to 5 business days, require payment of the undisputed portion immediately, and add a fast‑track dispute resolution mechanism (e.g., mediation within 5 business days) to resolve disputes promptly.

findings.quoted_text: The parties acknowledge that the description of the Services is intended to identify the principal workstreams. Minor clarifications may be made through ordinary project communications, provided that such clarification does not materially increase the workload.
findings.explanation: The clause allows the client to request minor clarifications that could effectively add work without triggering a formal change order, opening the door to unplanned effort and cost overruns.
findings.suggested_change: Define "minor clarification" with concrete limits (e.g., no more than 2 hours of additional effort) and require any request exceeding that limit to be documented as a change order with associated fees.

findings.quoted_text: Any post-launch support period is limited to the duration and scope stated in the commercial schedule. Requests outside that scope are handled as new Services or change requests.
findings.explanation: The clause attempts to limit support, but the definition of "scope" is vague and could allow the client to claim additional work falls within the original scope, leading to extra unpaid effort.
findings.suggested_change: Add a clear statement that any work beyond the listed milestones or the defined deliverables requires a written change order and will be billed at an agreed rate before work begins.

findings.explanation: Only three revision rounds are permitted, which protects you; however, the contract does not define what constitutes a "round," so the client might request numerous minor tweaks within each round, effectively creating unlimited revisions.
findings.suggested_change: Define a "revision round" as a single set of consolidated feedback addressing all items, and state that each round may not exceed a total of X hours or Y pages of changes.

findings.quoted_text: At handover, Contractor will provide the agreed source files, credentials or access instructions that Contractor is entitled to transfer, and available documentation.
findings.explanation: The clause obliges you to deliver all IP and source files at handover without linking delivery to receipt of the final payment, exposing you to the risk of transferring ownership before being fully compensated.
findings.suggested_change: Tie the handover of IP to the receipt of the final milestone payment, e.g., "All source files and IP will be transferred upon payment of the final milestone invoice."

findings.explanation: The liability cap exceeds the total contract fee (USD 24,875), meaning you could be liable for damages that are significantly higher than what you are being paid, which could be financially burdensome.
findings.suggested_change: Reduce the liability cap to an amount equal to the total contract value or a multiple (e.g., 1.5 × fee) and carve out exceptions for gross negligence or willful misconduct.

findings.explanation: Net 30 is standard, but the contract does not specify interest compounding or a grace period, and a 1% monthly interest can accumulate quickly if the client delays payment, impacting cash flow.
findings.suggested_change: Specify that interest is calculated on a simple annual basis (e.g., 12% per annum) and include a 5‑day grace period before interest accrues; also consider adding an early‑payment discount to encourage timely payment.

content.subject: Proposed changes to the agreement
content.body:
Hi,

I hope you’re well. Before I sign the agreement, I’d like to propose a few adjustments for mutual clarity:

- The termination clause allows the client to end the agreement without notice or payment for work performed. I propose adding a requirement for at least 30 days written notice and payment for all completed work, approved expenses, and earned milestones up to the termination date.
- The IP transfer clause shifts ownership of each deliverable to the client upon delivery, even if payment is pending. I suggest making the transfer conditional on receipt of payment for the corresponding invoice (or at least a specified percentage, e.g., 50% of the deliverable fee).
- The payment terms state invoices are Net 30 with 1% monthly interest on late payments. To improve cash flow, I recommend changing the term to Net 15 and increasing the late‑payment interest to 1.5% per month (or the maximum allowed) plus a reasonable fixed late fee.
- The dispute clause permits the client to withhold payment for up to 15 days while disputing an invoice. I propose shortening the dispute period to five business days, requiring immediate payment of the undisputed portion, and adding a fast‑track mediation process within five business days.
- The services description clause allows minor clarifications that could add work without a formal change order. I recommend defining “minor clarification” as no more than two hours of additional effort and requiring any request beyond that to be documented as a change order with associated fees.
- The post‑launch support clause limits support to the scope in the commercial schedule, but the definition of “scope” is vague. I suggest adding a clear statement that any work beyond the listed milestones or defined deliverables requires a written change order and will be billed at an agreed rate before work begins.
- The handover clause obliges delivery of source files and IP at handover without linking it to final payment. I propose tying the transfer of all source files and IP to receipt of the final milestone payment.
- The liability cap of USD 35,000 exceeds the total contract value of USD 24,875. I recommend reducing the cap to an amount equal to the total contract value (or 1.5 × the fee) with exceptions for gross negligence or willful misconduct.

Please let me know if these revisions are acceptable. I look forward to moving ahead.

Thank you
